title: bug: the pinned-corpus SHA-forgery arm has a 2.9x margin on the same 5s default and is the next arm to red the root lane
description:
HANDED ON FROM task-4a9d95cfc26a413cae7e8c07ecc1129b (the moved-tree arm in the SAME FILE, fixed there). That row's DoD 3 forbade changing this arm's budget, so it is filed rather than fixed. dependsOn task-4a9d95cf because both edits land in the same file and must not collide in the shared worktree.

THE ARM: packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts, "never lets a caller-supplied SHA stand in for observed Git authority" (was :186, now ~:200 after task-4a9d95cf's two hunks).

MEASURED, TWICE, ON THIS HOST, against vitest's DEFAULT 5000ms with no explicit budget on the `it`:
- 1721ms under fleet load (architect-5385678f, plan time for task-4a9d95cf) — a 2.9x margin.
- 280 / 287 / 290 / 632ms idle (worker-bcaa6d5e, 2026-09-08 ~19:20Z, four standalone runs).

WHY IT WILL FLAKE. Its sibling in the same file was measured at 693ms idle, 2317ms loaded, and >5000ms in the filing that opened task-4a9d95cf — a ~15x spread over IDENTICAL bytes. The variable is host contention on git subprocess spawns, not work: task-4a9d95cf's phase timers put 98.7% of the sibling's duration in NINE git spawns. This arm calls the same `newCorpusRepo` helper (three git spawns) plus four production authority observations. A 2.9x margin against a 15x observed spread is the same bet the sibling lost.

WHY IT MATTERS: root `pnpm test` is a DoD-1 leg for many rows on this board. A red that belongs to nobody's diff burns a full-suite run plus a gate lease every time it fires, and teaches readers to discount root reds.

THE FIX SHAPE, already proven on the sibling: an explicit per-`it` third-argument budget sized from a fresh measurement, with a comment naming the number AND the measurement it came from. NOT a retry, NOT an exclusion, NOT a raised global `testTimeout` — all three were rejected on task-4a9d95cf for reasons recorded in its planningNotes.

ALSO WORTH MEASURING WHILE HERE, but only if it does not change the other arms' behaviour: `newCorpusRepo` (:41-53) issues THREE git spawns (`init`, `add`, `commit`) per call and is the single largest cost in every arm that uses it (:92 DIRTY_REPO sweep case, the moved-tree arm, and this one). task-4a9d95cf could not touch it because its DoD protected the other eleven arms' behaviour. A row that owns the whole file could.
definitionOfDone: The SHA-forgery arm carries an explicit per-`it` budget sized from a fresh measurement of its own duration, with the number and its measurement recorded in a comment: not a retry, not an exclusion, not a raised global testTimeout.

At least ten consecutive standalone runs of packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts are green with both the `Tests N passed` count line AND the arm's own duration in ms quoted per run, plus the min/max/median, because ten greens at a duration near the budget prove nothing.

A mutation drill proves the budget is load-bearing: set it below the measured duration and the arm times out again; and the arm still refuses at CORPUS_ROOT_UNSET and CORPUS_ROOT_DIRTY at PRE_FREEZE_AUDIT, so the budget did not make a broken arm green.
The other eleven arms in the file keep their current behaviour and budgets, including the moved-tree arm's `}, 30_000);` landed by task-4a9d95cf.

Root `pnpm test` run under the full-suite-gate, with its exit code and `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim; any foreign red attributed by path against the merge-base baseline and disclosed, never fixed in-line.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE BEFORE YOU SIZE. NO EDITS.

Confirm the target and take the fresh measurement DoD 1 requires. The command that runs this file ALONE and prints each arm's own duration is:

  pnpm exec vitest run --root . packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts --reporter=verbose

DO NOT USE `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test -- pre-freeze-pinned-documents`. Measured at plan time: the trailing filter does NOT filter — it ran all 25 files in the benchmark package, and the same idiom ran all 49 in scheduler. A sample taken that way is not standalone and DoD 2 is silently unmet.

CONFIRM, by reading:
- The arm is at :200, "never lets a caller-supplied SHA stand in for observed Git authority", body :200-211, closing `});` with NO third argument.
- `grep -n "^  }, " packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts` returns exactly ONE line today — :194, the sibling's `}, 30_000);` landed by task-4a9d95cf. Record that count; it is the before half of DoD 4's proof.
- The file holds TWELVE arms and the count line is `Tests 12 passed (12)`: one sweep-roster arm at :130, eight generated at :137-150, the moved-tree arm at :158, this one, the portability arm at :217.

THE COST IS GIT SPAWNS, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS ALREADY DONE. `observeCorpusGit` (pre-freeze-pinned-documents.ts:121-143) issues exactly TWO git subprocesses per observation, `rev-parse --verify HEAD` and `status --porcelain=v2 -z --untracked-files=all`, both through the module's only `execFileSync` at :80-86. `newCorpusRepo` adds three. So this arm is 3 + 2 (:209) + 2 (:210) = SEVEN, its :206 call spawning nothing because the variable is deleted and `resolveCorpusRoot` refuses first. The sibling is NINE by the same count, which is exactly what task-4a9d95cf measured with phase timers — so the model is confirmed, and you do not need to re-instrument.

PLAN-TIME REFERENCE, quiet host, one run: this arm 205ms, the moved-tree sibling 251ms, the DIRTY_REPO sweep case 203ms, the whole file 859ms. Consistent with the filing's 280/287/290/632ms idle and 1721ms loaded. Take your own numbers; these are for recognising a wrong one.

Do NOT touch `newCorpusRepo` (:41-53). Three arms call it and DoD 4 protects two of them.

LAND THE BUDGET AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES IT.

Change the arm's closing `});` at :211 to a third-argument budget, and put a comment immediately above it — inside the `it` body, where the sibling's sits at :189-193 — carrying the number AND the measurement it came from. DoD 1 wants both: a budget with no recorded measurement is a picked number, and the next reader has no way to tell whether it is still right.

THE NUMBER. Default to `30_000`, matching the sibling at :194, unless your own measurement argues otherwise. Same file, same helper, same host, same contention source; one budget spelled twice reads better than two numbers a later reader has to reconcile. Do not derive it by ratio from the sibling's spawn count — the budget is sized to the contention TAIL, which is a property of the host, not of the seven-versus-nine spawn difference.

WHAT THE COMMENT MUST CARRY: your fresh idle duration, the loaded observation from the filing (1721ms under fleet load, a 2.9x margin on the 5s default), the ~15x spread the sibling measured over IDENTICAL bytes, and the resulting margin. State plainly that what varies is host contention on git subprocess spawns, not work — that is the fact which makes a large budget correct rather than lazy.

WHAT YOU MAY NOT DO, by DoD 1: no retry, no exclusion, no raised global `testTimeout`. `vitest.config.ts` is not an owned path and must stay untouched. All three were rejected on task-4a9d95cf for reasons in its planningNotes.

NOTHING ELSE IN THE FILE CHANGES. Not the other eleven arms, not their budgets, not `newCorpusRepo`, not the sweep roster, not the sibling's `}, 30_000);` at :194.

TEN CONSECUTIVE STANDALONE RUNS, WITH THE NUMBERS THAT MAKE THEM MEAN SOMETHING (DoD 2).

Run the step-1 command ten times in a row and record, PER RUN: the `Tests N passed` count line and this arm's own duration in ms as the verbose reporter prints it. Then report min, max and median across the ten.

DoD 2 says in its own words why: ten greens at a duration near the budget prove nothing. The evidence is the MARGIN, and the count is only what makes the margin repeatable. Compute the margin explicitly as budget divided by the worst observed duration.

STATE THE HOST CONDITION HONESTLY. If the host was quiet for all ten, say so and say that the margin rather than the count is carrying the claim — that is exactly what task-4a9d95cf's row did and what its QA credited. If you can get even one run under real fleet load, it is worth more than three more quiet ones; note which runs were which.

QUOTE THE COUNT LINE VERBATIM. `Test Files 1 passed (1)` and `Tests 12 passed (12)`. A vitest run that matched no files prints "No test files found" and EXITS 0, and a filter that matched nothing exits 0 too — the count line is the only discriminator, never the exit code.

Put the per-run table in a task COMMENT, not in the completion summary: the summary truncates silently at 2000 chars and a severed table reads as a skipped gate.

TWO DRILLS AND THE ELEVEN-ARMS PROOF (DoD 3, DoD 4).

PREFER A PROCESS-LOCAL MUTATION. task-4a9d95cf drilled this exact file through a throwaway `--config` transform rather than writing to disk: it needs no gate lease, it cannot collide with a peer's run, and it leaves the tree byte-identical. Use it. If you do write to disk, both files are TRACKED and the checkout is shared, so back the path up out of tree under a name carrying BOTH this task id and your worker id, take the SHA256 from the LIVE file before mutating, restore by copying the backup back, and prove it by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A `%TEMP%` path keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage from an earlier session and certify a restore that destroyed the row.

DRILL (i) — THE BUDGET IS LOAD-BEARING. Set the new budget below the measured duration and confirm the arm reds with a TIMEOUT naming that reduced number, the way the sibling's drill produced `Test timed out in 200ms`. A budget nothing can fail against is not evidence.

DRILL (ii) — THE BUDGET DID NOT MAKE A BROKEN ARM GREEN. Mutate the PRODUCTION refusal in packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.ts so the arm's expected codes no longer come back, and confirm it reds ON THE ASSERTION — not on a timeout — at both conditions DoD 3 names: `CORPUS_ROOT_UNSET` at :206 with the variable deleted, and `CORPUS_ROOT_DIRTY` at :209 with the layer `PRE_FREEZE_AUDIT` at :210. The two conditions take different paths through the module — UNSET refuses in `resolveCorpusRoot` before any git spawn, DIRTY refuses after `observeCorpusGit` returns — so a single mutation may not reach both; drill whichever way reaches each, and say which mutation produced which red. Assertion-red versus timeout-red is the whole point of this drill.

DoD 4 — THE OTHER ELEVEN ARMS ARE UNCHANGED. `grep -n "^  }, " packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts` must now return exactly TWO lines: the sibling's `}, 30_000);` and yours. Quote both. Pair it with `git diff --stat` on the file and confirm every hunk is inside the one `it` — the sibling row landed +16/-2 on one file and its QA used exactly this pair as the proof.

THE ROOT LANE UNDER THE GATE, WITH THE FOREIGN RED ATTRIBUTED (DoD 5), THEN THE ADVERSARIAL PASS.

Acquire the `full-suite-gate` resource with moe.acquire_resource before running root, and release it after. It was free at plan time (`holders: []`, `queue: []`) but a peer can take it; if it is held, wait for the grant rather than running root alongside another full suite — concurrent full runs are what produces the contention this whole row is about.

Run root `pnpm test` and quote the exit code AND the `Test Files N passed` count line verbatim.

EXPECT A FOREIGN RED, AND DO NOT FIX IT. Measured at plan time, reproducing at HEAD: `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` fails with `boundary scan failed for apps\daemon\src\deployment\deploy-candidate-environment.ts: Error: unterminated quoted source token`, thrown at that test's :327; scheduler alone reports `Test Files 1 failed | 48 passed (49)`, `Tests 1 failed | 1737 passed (1738)`. It is the same red task-4a9d95cf's QA confirmed foreign and routed to the governor, and it lives in packages/scheduler and apps/daemon — neither owned by this row. Attribute it the way global rail 3 requires: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, then at HEAD, the delta intersected with this row's owned paths, and that intersection must be EMPTY. Disclose the red verbatim with its exact failing lines and paths. DoD 5 asks for the run and the attribution, not for exit 0, and inventing a pass remains forbidden.

Note also that root `pnpm test` does NOT cover apps/**: if you say anything about repo-wide green, either run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and quote their count lines, or say "root lane only, apps/** not covered". This row owns nothing under apps/**, so the second is the honest and sufficient answer.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: does the arm still FAIL for the right reason, or did the budget turn a real defect green — what does drill (ii) actually say? If the host had been loaded during the ten runs, would the sample have changed the budget? Did anything outside the one `it` move — check the diff, not your memory? Is the number in the comment the number in the code? And the question the filing poses: after this change, is there any remaining arm in this file whose margin against its budget is smaller than the ~15x spread this host has been measured to produce — and if so, is it worth a comment on this row rather than a new one?

comments.content:
A THIRD ARM OF THE SAME CLASS, FOUND WHILE ATTRIBUTING ROOT RED ON task-4a9d95cf. Measured 2026-09-08 by worker-bcaa6d5e. Recording it here rather than opening another row, because whoever plans this row is already holding the "5s default vs. load-dependent work" problem.

`tools/packaging/pack-command.test.ts` around :649. worker-9dcd2d4f's root baseline at 18:42:13Z reported it as a root-lane failure: "pack-command.test.ts:649 timeout5000ms". I re-ran that file STANDALONE at HEAD minutes ago and it PASSED — `Tests 1 failed | 87 passed (88)`, where the single failure was the unrelated `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` boundary scan, not pack-command. Red under fleet load, green standalone, same bytes: that is the signature this whole thread is about.

`grep -n "}, [0-9_]*);" tools/packaging/pack-command.test.ts` returns NOTHING — the file has no explicit per-`it` budget anywhere, so every arm in it races vitest's 5000ms default. The arms around :649 hash a real executable via `pinnedCargoExecutable()` and compare a pinned sha256, which is load-dependent file I/O on a binary.

NOT IN THIS ROW'S SCOPE AS FILED (this row names the pinned-corpus file), and I am deliberately NOT widening it — but a planner who wants to fix the class rather than one instance should consider whether the two belong in one row. If they are split, the pack-command one needs its own row; leaving it in this comment alone will lose it.

Method that worked on task-4a9d95cf and is worth reusing here: measure with `--reporter=verbose` for per-arm ms; get the write/spawn account with phase timers surfaced through a deliberate failing `expect` (console.log is swallowed in this repo's vitest runs); and run mutation drills PROCESS-LOCAL via a throwaway `--config` with a Vite `transform` plugin, so nothing is mutated on the shared tree while a peer holds full-suite-gate.

comments.content:
Architect investigation, fresh foreground measurement on 2026-09-08, no source edits: command run THREE consecutive times: pnpm exec vitest run packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts --reporter=verbose --slowTestThreshold=0 --no-color. Each EXIT0, Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 12 passed (12). Target 'never lets a caller-supplied SHA stand in for observed Git authority' durations: 1092 / 386 / 422 ms; min386, max1092, median422. These are planning samples, NOT the ten delivered-tree runs required by DoD2. Proposed arm-local 30000ms budget gives 27.47x measured maximum / 28.908 seconds remaining. Use 30s as deliberately generous spawn-contention allowance, not a promise about host worst-case; former 5s gives only4.58x this fresh max. Historical15x spread belongs to the sibling and must remain identified as such.

Measured source: target arm :200-211 has no explicit timeout and is synchronous. It launches SEVEN Git processes, not four production observations: fixture init/add/commit plus two dirty-root forge() calls at209/210, each rev-parse+status. The unset-root call has no git work. Actual installed Vitest4.1.10 checks elapsed time on resolve including synchronous callback return (@vitest/runner/dist/chunk-artifact.js:2284-2293 and2305-2311), so a below-duration per-it mutation can timeout without adding synthetic async work. No helper optimization or production change needed. Existing unset-root assertion pins code but NOT layer; minimal owning-arm fix should save that existing result once and assert CORPUS_ROOT_UNSET+PRE_FREEZE_AUDIT together, preserving the existing dirty calls/assertions and zero-argument arity checks.

Dependency task-4a9d95cf is landed at8b78572535058daef8ddf1d3f55d0e5f33c3bd1a and still REVIEW in get_context; dependsOn already gates WORKING until DONE. Its completionSummary documents same-file predecessor; current owned path is clean. No wait/block or reordering required at planning time. Moved-tree arm's30_000 and path-gated fs mock are present; preserve verbatim along with other eleven arms. Full-tree title/filename/arity search has no other source asserting consumers. No new package imports/edge/exports/rosters needed.

Proposed four-step plan: (1) record claim baseline/current host measurements and red controls using task-keyed process-local Vite transform; (2) add only target third-argument30000/comment + missing unset-layer pin; (3) one final verification with ten consecutive standalone file runs and every printed target ms/count/exit, min/max/median/margin, @moe/benchmark test/typecheck, and required root/repository legs under full-suite-gate with merge-base path attribution, preserving all other arms; (4) one adversarial review including below-duration timeout and production refusal-code/layer mutations, confirm source hashes unchanged by process-local drills and no scratch survives. A disposable root config is a harness only, removed and never committed. Do not widen to newCorpusRepo or pack-command.ts; unrelated timeout comments stay follow-ups, not an excuse for scope growth.

REPL scope/approach confirmation requested before submit_plan. No response yet; task remains PLANNING rather than falsely blocked on a dependency already delivered. This comment is investigation/draft, NOT an approved plan.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
ACCEPTED — an explicit per-`it` third-argument budget on the SHA-forgery arm alone, sized from a fresh measurement, with the number and its measurement in a comment. This is the shape task-4a9d95cf proved on the sibling arm 8 lines above (`}, 30_000);` at :194) and the filing names it. Match that number unless the fresh measurement argues otherwise: same file, same helper, same host, same contention source, and one budget spelled twice reads better than two numbers a later reader has to reconcile.

REJECTED — a retry, an exclusion, or a raised global `testTimeout` in vitest.config.ts. All three were rejected on task-4a9d95cf and DoD 1 forbids them by name. A retry hides the spread instead of surviving it; an exclusion deletes coverage; a global raise slows every genuine hang in the repo to the new bound.

REJECTED — optimising `newCorpusRepo` (:41-53) down from three git spawns. The filing floats it as optional and DoD 4 protects the other eleven arms; two of them (the DIRTY_REPO sweep case and the moved-tree arm) call that helper, so any change there is a change to their behaviour under exactly the contention this row exists to survive, and the sibling's budget comment is calibrated against the current helper. The DELIVERY BIAS rail says take the smallest production-reachable slice: the budget is the whole fix. If the helper is ever worth cutting, it is its own row against all three call sites at once, not a passenger on this one. Measured cost for the record: the helper is ~200ms of the arm's ~205ms.

REJECTED — sizing the budget by ratio from the sibling. The arm makes SEVEN git spawns to the sibling's nine (arithmetic in codebaseInsights), so a ratio would say ~23s. But the budget is not sized to the work; it is sized to the contention TAIL, and the tail is a property of the host, not of the spawn count. DoD 1 asks for a fresh measurement of this arm's own duration, so take one and state the margin against it.

planningNotes.risks:
1. TEN GREENS PROVE NOTHING ON A QUIET HOST. DoD 2 says so in its own words. The sibling's QA accepted ten greens BECAUSE the margin was 43x and the row said plainly that the host was quiet for all ten. The evidence is the MARGIN plus the min/max/median, not the count. Report the quiet-or-loaded condition honestly.

2. THE WRONG COMMAND SILENTLY WIDENS THE SAMPLE. `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- <name>` does not filter; it runs the whole package. Measured at plan time on two packages. A worker who uses it has not run the file standalone and DoD 2 is unmet while every number looks plausible.

3. A FILTER THAT MATCHES NOTHING EXITS 0, and so does "No test files found". The `Test Files 1 passed (1)` and `Tests 12 passed (12)` lines are the only discriminators; the exit code is not.

4. THE BUDGET DRILL CAN PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON. Drill (i) must red with a TIMEOUT message naming the reduced budget. Drill (ii) must red on the ASSERTION, not on a timeout — that is what proves the budget did not paper over a broken arm, and it is exactly the distinction task-4a9d95cf's QA credited.

5. DRILL RESTORE ON A SHARED TREE. Both files are TRACKED and the worktree is shared. Prefer the process-local `--config` transform task-4a9d95cf used on this same file: it needs no lease and mutates nothing. If anything is written to disk, back it up out of tree under a name carrying BOTH this task id and your worker id, take the SHA256 from the LIVE file before mutating, and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A `%TEMP%` path keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage from a previous session.

6. `newCorpusRepo` IS SHARED BY THREE ARMS. Editing it to save spawns touches the DIRTY_REPO sweep case and the moved-tree arm, whose budget comment is calibrated against the current helper. DoD 4 protects both. Leave it alone.

7. THE FOREIGN ROOT RED IS EXPECTED, NOT A BLOCKER. It reproduces at HEAD right now and belongs to packages/scheduler and apps/daemon. Do not fix it, do not block on it, and do not let it become an excuse for skipping the root run: DoD 5 wants the run, its exit code, its count line, and the attribution.
